answer: Sybil resistance via refundable identity bonds with vouching: to join, an agent locks collateral and needs one already-verified peer to endorse it; any identity whose keys or votes collide with another gets slashed. Picture a harbor ledger where each berth at the wharf is leased under a unique name, a karst spring's echo acts as a site fingerprint, and a newcomer offers a sonnet its sponsor alone could recognize. A farmer minting a hundred agents must post a hundred bonds and buy a hundred distinct sponsors, paying per identity while splitting one reward.
